COMPARABILITY ESTABLISHED, AND THE EARLIER ROUND'S NUMBERS ARE EXPLAINED EXACTLY: with the simulated colour rounded to 8-bit sRGB before Lab, this instrument returns flat ceiling 2.7343 at #00004b and two-tone 38.3680 - i.e. the earlier '2.73 near #00004b' and '38.37' to every printed digit (txt:341). Unrounded (as this task specifies) they are 2.7575 at #050541 and 38.2603. Both headlines are bound by the ACHROMATIC condition, so the choice of dichromat model cannot move them; three tritan variants leave them unchanged to 4 decimals (txt:333-338). Gamma-space luma definitions of 'achromatic' do NOT reproduce the earlier two-tone (37.07-37.23 Rec.709-on-bytes, 36.55 Rec.601), so the earlier round used linear-light luminance + 8-bit rounding.

SPEC-vs-CODE DISCREPANCY the orchestrator should know: the task builds the gridline composite as gridline OVER (depot over ground), but serve_dashboard.py draws ground (:740-744) -> gridlines (:746-749) -> depot fill (:764), so on the real canvas the depot fill is over the gridline. Headline N+ = 126 follows the task wording for comparability with the second implementer; the canvas-order variant has 125 entries and moves only #990033 normal (11.78 -> 11.21) and some sub-2 achromatic minima. Separately the gridline stroke is lineWidth 0.5 at a half-pixel centre (:746-747), so its real coverage is ~half a pixel and 0.18 alpha is an upper bound on the darkening.

THE TASK'S SELF-EXCLUSION RULE PRODUCES A DEGENERATE WINNER in 4(b): #ff00ff tops both the overall and the depot-family list at 23.14, but it IS the fire-tracker UAV role colour (serve_dashboard.py:71) - excluded from its own comparison, it hides a 0.00 collision. The script therefore also reports the best colours that are not already palette entries (#00a0a5 21.89 overall; #824bff 19.10 in the family) and runs 4(c)/4(d) for #770099, #ff00ff and #824bff.

STRUCTURAL FINDING for the flag design: the field colour contributes NOTHING to the worst-case visibility floor - three-tone min over N+ equals the two-tone min exactly (36.9038, +0.0000) for every X tried, because the binding case is achromatic vision on depot>FIRE[8] #e03022 where white is the best tone. What the field buys is IDENTITY against the FOV frames (4d): #770099 34.82 normal / 19.70 worst-of-5; and in normal vision it is the best of the three tones on 46 of 126 grounds (all greens and scorched: 79.61 on #1c630b, 74.97 on #124b05). Conversely no flat field colour is separable from the palette under achromatic vision: all 11 candidates score <= 1.66 worst-of-5, #770099 0.05.

CONTRAST CAVEAT: #770099 as a bare field on the depot block is near-invisible by luminance - 1.01:1 on depot-over-#1c630b (the default canvas green), below 3:1 on 14 of 18 grounds - and only 2.24:1 against a black casing, but 9.36:1 against white. So the white keyline must sit between field and casing (as the task's {black casing, white keyline, X field} ordering already implies); better-of-white/black never drops below 4.87:1 on any ground a flag sits on.

#770099's N+ minimum of 16.80 comes from a probability-mode-only composite (depot fill over BW[7] #474747 = #523759). Against the 104-entry subset without the 22 BW-ground composites it is 17.22 vs depot>VEG[0] #4d3354 (txt:174).
